title: hodd/identity/grants.yaml
description: The federation grant registry (plan 58, 'Several Ymirs, one company'): every explicit grant by which one operator's Ymir shares a company namespace with another's. Read by src/ymir_runtime/grants.py through the config layer (kind 'grants'). The realm law (Rule 05) is a semantic check, not a shape: a grant that crosses operators must carry a signature from EACH party's Heimdall, and src/ymir_runtime/grants.py refuses one that does not. `card` is deliberately the SAME shape as the shared agent-card contract (packages/contracts AgentInterface: protocol · endpoint · signed) — one contract, never a second.

operator.description: the local operator this registry belongs to; never required, so a heart may carry the whole company's grants

card.description: the shared A2A agent-card interface (packages/contracts AgentInterface) — protocol + endpoint + whether the binding is signed

endpoint.description: where the party's card + JSON-RPC are served

signed.description: does this party's card carry a Heimdall signature?

ymir.description: the Ymir instance's identity (its A2A name)

operator.description: the human/company operator the Ymir belongs to; the realm boundary is drawn between operators

heimdall.description: the key id of the operator's Heimdall that signs this side of the grant

signer.description: the Heimdall key id that made this signature — must be one of the parties

alg.description: the signing algorithm; Heimdall signs ed25519/JWS

key_id.description: the key the signature verifies against

sig.description: the base64url JWS signature over the grant body

grant_id.description: the stable id of this grant; a replayed id is refused, never silently applied

namespace.description: the company namespace this grant opens — the unit Skuld stores rows under and the journal scopes entries to

issued.description: ISO 8601 instant the grantor issued the grant

expires.description: ISO 8601 instant the grant lapses; empty/absent means no expiry

signatures.description: the Heimdall signatures; a cross-operator grant requires one per party
